speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our evaluation, have you experienced multiple fractures from minor traumas, and if so, at what ages did they occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Lipoid CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (labial fusion, clitoromegaly), severe acne, hirsutism, and bone fragility suggests a chronic mineralocorticoid deficiency affecting bone mineralization and delayed puberty. Have you experienced episodes of salt wasting, such as vomiting, dehydration, or low blood pressure, particularly in infancy?
